sources.title: Semitic, Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.note: Defines Semitic as a language group, lists ancient and living members, and identifies Proto-Semitic as hypothetical.

sources.title: Case in Semitic: introduction to reconstruction
sources.note: Oxford account of comparative reconstruction, data limits and a fluid understanding of proto-languages.

sources.title: Arabic as a Semitic language
sources.note: Cambridge history identifying Akkadian as the earliest attested Semitic language and distinguishing later branches.

sources.title: The Ancient Languages of Mesopotamia, Egypt and Aksum
sources.note: Cambridge linguistic guide distinguishing Sumerian, Akkadian, Eblaite and other ancient languages and scripts.

sources.title: Aryan, Holocaust Encyclopedia
sources.note: Institutional history of how linguistic labels including Semite were falsely reinterpreted as racial categories.

sources.title: The Genomic History of the Bronze Age Southern Levant
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ancient-DNA study of 73 individuals from five southern Levantine sites and heterogeneous ancestry.

sources.title: Genomic insights into the origin of farming in the ancient Near East
sources.note: Ancient-DNA evidence that early Near Eastern farming populations were differentiated and descended from local foragers.

sources.title: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
sources.note: UNESCO synthesis of third-millennium eastern Arabian settlements, tombs, towers, quarries, water works and copper exchange.

sources.title: Settlement and Cemetery of Umm an-Nar Island
sources.note: UNESCO account of the 2600 to 2000 BCE settlement, communal tombs, craft and Gulf connections.

sources.title: Arabian Peninsula, 8000 to 2000 B.C.
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum chronology of Arabian herding, crops, mining, craft, exchange and regional variation.

sources.title: Bat Archaeological Project
sources.note: Penn Museum field-project account of surveys, settlements, cemeteries and Bronze Age towers at Bat.

sources.title: The Bronze Age Towers at Bat, Sultanate of Oman
sources.note: Museum monograph summary of excavation, GIS survey, radiocarbon dating and debated tower functions.

sources.title: The recreated reed boat Magan
sources.note: Penn Museum experimental reconstruction of a bitumen-covered reed boat and Bronze Age Gulf route.

sources.title: Plant, pigment, and bone processing at Jebel Oraf
sources.note: Peer-reviewed use-wear analysis of grinding tools and the mixed pastoral, hunting and plant-processing economy of northern Arabia.

sources.title: Pastoral and plant products in Early Bronze Age southeastern Arabian pottery
sources.note: Lipid residues, archaeobotany and zooarchaeology showing dairying and varied inland and coastal foods.

sources.title: Human occupation of Umm Jirsan lava tube
sources.note: Multiproxy evidence for shade, water, herding routes, hunting and episodic cave use in northern Arabia.

sources.title: Mapping past human land use using archaeological data
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of southwest Arabian pastoralism, cultivation and early runoff irrigation.

sources.title: South Arabia monument landscapes and climate resilience
sources.note: Radiocarbon-informed evidence for mobile pastoralists, Bronze Age tombs and adaptation to aridity in Dhofar.

sources.title: The mustatils: cult and monumentality in Neolithic north-western Arabia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed excavation, radiocarbon dating and interpretation of animal offerings and procession architecture.

sources.title: Much ado about nothing: the 4.2 kya event and subsistence
sources.note: Stable-isotope study cautioning against a single megadrought-collapse story across northern Mesopotamia.

sources.title: Household Archaeology at Arad and Ai in Early Bronze Age II
sources.note: House plans, pottery and ecological comparison at two southern Levantine Early Bronze Age towns.

sources.title: Household Studies in Complex Societies
sources.note: Scholarly guide to the possibilities and limits of reconstructing households from buildings, objects, texts and micro-remains.

sources.title: Subsistence, Trade, and Social Change in Early Bronze Age Palestine
sources.note: Regional study of crops, herds, exchange, settlements, courtyards and unequal household evidence.

sources.title: Fishing and fish consumption at Tel Bet Yerah, 3200 to 2700 BC
sources.note: Systematically sampled fish remains and gear showing changing local food use during southern Levantine urbanization.

sources.title: Beyond Babylon: Art, Trade, and Diplomacy in the Second Millennium B.C.
sources.note: Museum synthesis of exchange, diplomacy, tribute and distinctive courts at Mari, Ebla and Byblos.

sources.title: Art of the Ancient Near East: a resource for educators
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum educational survey distinguishing Mesopotamian and Syrian cities, arts, writing and trade.

sources.title: Mesopotamian City Life
sources.note: Penn Museum account of named urban Mesopotamian schooling, work, women, children, seals and toys.

sources.title: Back to School in Babylonia
sources.note: Excavation-based Old Babylonian study of House F at Nippur and its scribal curriculum.

sources.title: Women, Gender, and Religion in Ancient Mesopotamia
sources.note: ISAC discussion of patriarchy alongside women in property, economy, religion and elite scribal education.

sources.title: Medicine in the third and second millennium BCE
sources.note: ORACC/British Museum account of localized Sumerian and Old Babylonian medical records and plant remedies.

sources.title: Techniques of Mesopotamian medicine
sources.note: ORACC/British Museum guide to bandages, salves, baths, potions and other documented treatments.

sources.title: From lunch to latrine: sanitation in past populations
sources.note: Scholarly review of early Mesopotamian deep-pit toilets, household waste and limits of urban sanitation.

sources.title: Old Akkadian royal inscription of Sargon
sources.note: Primary digital edition of a named Old Akkadian royal victory inscription, used only as outside-polygon comparison.

sources.title: ePSD2 entry for Akkadian sharrum, king
sources.note: Primary lexical record showing a named Akkadian equivalent, not a Proto-Semitic or umbrella-wide word sample.

sources.title: Slaves and Households in the Near East
sources.note: Scholarly studies of Old Babylonian household institutions and domestic female slavery.

sources.title: Sometimes Defence is Just an Excuse
sources.note: Peer-reviewed caution that Early Bronze Age southern Levantine walls had social and symbolic as well as defensive roles.

sources.title: Chronology of the Early Bronze Age in the Southern Levant
sources.note: Bayesian modeling of 420 radiocarbon dates and site-dependent Early Bronze Age transitions.

sources.title: New excavations at Tel Erani
sources.note: Field evidence for fortifications, radiocarbon dating and early urbanization in the southern Levant.

sources.title: Canaanite dialects
sources.note: Cambridge linguistic account of second-millennium Canaanite evidence and Proto-Canaanite inscriptions.

sources.title: Proto-Sinaitic inscribed figure from Serabit el-Khadim
sources.note: British Museum object record locating Proto-Sinaitic signs among local workers at the Sinai turquoise mines.

sources.title: Alphabet Origins: From Kipling to Sinai
sources.note: Museum history of the Serabit discoveries, acrophony and the early second-millennium alphabet.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: Modern linguistic umbrella over diverse Arabian and southern Levantine communities; never one race, nation, culture or state.

batchIdentityNotes: The indexed display name is “Semitic-speaking peoples,” with alias “Semites”; public copy treats Semitic strictly as a language-family label.
The imported summary overstates common ancestry, subsistence and geography and is replaced by a qualified card.
Exact geometry covers Arabia, Sinai and the southern Levant, while the atlas assigns Akkadian Mesopotamia and Ebla to other layers.
At 2000 BCE Canaan leaves the target polygon despite Canaanite being Semitic, exposing a taxonomy conflict rather than a language frontier.
The 1500 BCE endpoint assigns tested places to several anachronistic labels and is preserved as an atlas seam, never a successor map.
Proto-Semitic is explicitly reconstructed; archaeology, ancient DNA, material culture and language are never collapsed into one identity.
Later and outside-polygon Mesopotamian texts are labeled comparisons, not target-wide practices.
A tiny written sample is included only for the localized Proto-Sinaitic mining community at Serabit el-Khadim inside the exact polygon and date range; it is not presented as an umbrella voice.
